FitPulse — Fitness Mobile App

Case Study UI/UX Designer

In short: a workplace wellness app that builds consistent workout habits out of short daily actions — structured plans, simple progress tracking, and challenges you can take on alone, with a team, or as a group.

Overview

FitPulse helps people build consistent workout habits with structured plans and simple progress tracking. Users earn rewards by completing challenges and take part in solo, team, and group activities — turning wellbeing from something that competes with the working day into something that fits inside it.

Project

  • RoleUI/UX Designer
  • Duration6 months
  • TeamWorked under a Senior Designer
  • StatusPaused due to funding constraints

The app name and visual branding have been modified for portfolio presentation.

Brand Identity

The logo is a modern monogram carrying a pulse element — a shorthand for active living, tracking, and transformation through fitness.

Problem

Workplaces face declining productivity from stress, burnout, and excessive screen time. Long hours on a device erode focus, and busy schedules make healthy habits hard to hold onto.

Traditional wellness programmes rarely fix it. Engagement stays low and results stay weak, which feeds rising burnout, absenteeism, and cost — a widening gap between the effort put into wellbeing and any real productivity outcome.

Solution

A fitness and wellness engagement platform that improves productivity by embedding short, actionable health habits into the workday, using gamification and rewards to make them stick.

Design Process

01 · Research

Target user analysis

The B2B buyers for a fitness app are gyms and companies wanting to improve employee health. They look for simple, scalable tools that boost engagement and deliver measurable wellness results.

02 · Ideate

Aligning to real needs

Brainstorming and discussing solutions, then using the user research to refine the strongest direction rather than the most obvious one.

03 · Design

Structure, then surface

Wireframes to plan structure and flow, UI concepts to explore layout and functionality, then visual design to shape the final look and feel into something clean and easy to use.

Visual Identity

Brand visuals are energized. When people are engaged in their health, they perform better.

  • Clean, modern layouts
  • A green-fluorescent palette, for trust and energy
  • High contrast for readability
  • Card-based components for easy scanning

Typography

Outfit carries the whole interface — a geometric sans with enough range to hold a hierarchy without needing a second face.

Light 300 · Regular 400 · Medium 500 · Semi Bold 600

Colour Palette

Green leads, with a deep blue for grounding and three accents that keep challenge cards and rewards legible against it.

Green#749E93
Blue#2F444D
Pink#D98AE0
White#FFFFFF
Yellow#F8F1A3

Designing for Dubai

Dubai's workforce is genuinely diverse, which pushed the design toward neutral, inclusive choices — imagery and language that read the same across nationalities — while still keeping the regional relevance that made the challenges feel local rather than generic.

Result

Improved employee engagement through gamified challenges.

A scalable solution adaptable across companies.

Strong alignment between business goals and user needs.

Clear visibility of wellness metrics for HR teams.

Aligns business goals with user motivation — a practical, sustainable approach to workplace wellness in Dubai.
